title: Autotuning CuTe DSL Kernels
critical_patterns: Use grid search for exhaustive exploration of parameter combinations
Random search offers faster exploration for large parameter spaces
Bayesian optimization intelligently selects configurations using machine learning
Genetic algorithms evolve configurations over generations
Cache tuned parameters for reuse to avoid redundant computations
Tune parameters specific to problem sizes for optimal performance
constraints: Ensure parameter combinations do not exceed hardware limits
Tune on the target hardware for accurate results
Validate configurations to ensure they meet performance and correctness criteria
compressed_summary: Autotuning in CuTe DSL involves automatically finding optimal kernel parameters through various search strategies such as grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization, and genetic algorithms. These methods explore parameter spaces to minimize execution time and adapt configurations to specific hardware and problem sizes. Key parameters to tune include tile sizes, pipeline depth, and block size. Autotuning can significantly outperform manual tuning, offering 2-5× better configurations. Best practices include starting with a coarse grid search, refining with more targeted searches, caching results for reuse, and validating configurations for correctness. Constraints such as hardware limits and problem size specificity must be considered to ensure effective tuning. Tools like Bayesian optimization libraries and the OpenTuner framework can facilitate this process. The ultimate goal is to achieve optimal performance tailored to the specific hardware and problem characteristics, ensuring efficient execution across various scenarios.
